kind: A pilot at full size, one seed: depth by recurrence at equal parameters, with the energy it takes as an arm of its own.
why: The full-size gap is knowledge (full_size_word_heads.json, full_size_rate_pilot.json), and every part added beside the cells has failed to change it. Depth helps both models, but real levels cost parameters: depth 22 gains the stack 0.027 at twice the parameters. A looped stack runs some of its levels more than once with the same synapses (--stack-loop, results/event_lm/stack_loop/preregistered.json): more computation per parameter, as cortex computes by recurrence. On the test bed a loop of four middle levels run three times gained 0.047 over depth 6 at 6,000 updates (0.062 with a second seed), at equal parameters; a tied pass was worth about a third of a real level. That gain came with a pulse budget scaled with the passes; at the old budget the loop gained nothing, so the budget is a confound there. Daniel allowed a raised budget if it is what wins, as an arm of its own (docs/ROADMAP.md, rule 2), so this pilot separates the two.

arms.fs-loop6: --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000: levels 2 to 8 run twice with tied synapses, 18 level passes in all, and the budget scaled with the passes (310,000 times 18 / 11); 34,810,900 parameters, as the base
arms.fs-b507: --pulse-budget 507000 alone: the plain stack with the loop's budget and no loop, the control for the energy

base: fs-st6 of full_size_rate_pilot: the same recipe and seed at the budget of 310,000, 1.31985 on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as streams
training: full.sh KIND stack (v16's stack with forgetting slopes, windows of 512 bytes, batch 8, 24,000 updates, warmup 1,000, cosine over the run, seed 20001) at peak rate 6e-4, the plain pool, server GPU 0 after the full-size pair's stack arm; code v17n (97a2772)
measure: as full_size_rate_pilot: the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 unscored lead bytes, averaged weights, bits kept; fs-loop6 paired with fs-b507 and fs-b507 with fs-st6 by experiments/gap_by_piece.py (near 496, far 8,192); the pulses a byte and the price of the budget
reading: The loop's own gain is fs-b507 minus fs-loop6, at equal energy; the budget's gain is fs-st6 minus fs-b507. The loop earns a full-size run of 90,000 updates beside the pair if its own gain is at least 0.010 with its gain on new contexts above zero. The budget earns a place in the design if its gain is at least 0.010. Otherwise each is reported only. Recorded either way: every score, the gains by context, the pulses a byte, the training time of each arm, and how the energy compares with the plain stack's.
seen_before_recording: fs-st6 1.31985 and the rest of the full-size pilots; a 4-update CPU check of fs-loop6 at full size (finite, 34,810,900 parameters, about 500,000 pulses a byte). The test bed's loop pilot is the evidence above. No looped or raised-budget full-size run has trained.

amendment.change: fs-loop6 and fs-b507 train on GPU 1 in the night of 2026-11-23, after the two unit arms that are half trained there and before the full-size pair's Transformer arm, and no longer on GPU 0 after the pair's stack arm. Arms, recipe, code, seed, measure and reading are unchanged.

The loop is the largest gain that the test bed has measured for any part at equal parameters, so its full-size verdict is worth more this night than the pair's, which now comes about 15 hours later.
amendment.seen_before_amendment: No run of this pilot or of loop_with_data has started. Seen since the record: the laptop's gated and noisy arms and the proportional gate's check (proportional_gate_check.json); none bears on the loop.

stack_pulses_per_byte.energy: the loop and its control spend 1.63 times the plain stack's pulses a byte

training time, seconds for 1,500 updates.note: the loop takes 1.39 to 1.46 times the plain stack's time for 18 level passes in place of 11

result.how the arms trained: On GPU 1 on 2026-11-23 from 18:20 UTC, side by side. From 18:50 UTC (fs-loop6 from update 15,000, fs-b507 from update 7,500) both ran as programs of NVIDIA's multi-process service, a trial of sharing one GPU between two jobs; each was paused and resumed once for the switch. The service changes the pace, not the computation.

verdict.the loop: PASS: its own gain is 0.0189 where 0.010 was asked, and on new contexts it gains 0.0255 (interval 0.0227 to 0.0283). It earns a full-size run of 90,000 updates beside the pair.
verdict.the budget: FAIL: the plain stack with 507,000 pulses a byte is 0.0093 worse than with 310,000, where 0.010 better was asked; worse on new contexts by 0.0159 (interval 0.0133 to 0.0190). Reported only.

result.reading: Depth by recurrence is the first part at equal parameters that adds knowledge at full size. Against the plain stack at the old budget, which is the design it would replace, the looped stack is 0.0096 better on the whole and 0.0096 better on new contexts (interval 0.0069 to 0.0123), for 1.63 times the pulses and about 1.4 times the training time; against the lifted plain stack it is 0.0032 better. Its own gain at equal energy, 0.0189, is larger because the raised budget harms the control: the plain stack puts the added pulses into the same eleven levels, and its membranes saturate (3.0% of the cells' entries at their bound against 0.8%, 2.9% of the reads' against 0.3%, 11.4% of the other populations' against 1.5%). The loop spreads them over eighteen passes (1.4%, 1.6% and 2.2%). Open, and not separated by this pilot: whether the loop needs the raised budget at full size (on the test bed it gained nothing at the old budget), and whether the pool that lifts the ceiling adds to it, since the loop's reads saturate five times as often as the plain stack's.
